panel_overlap_note: Only 4/47 paired targets (ACLY, HDAC8, NFE2L1, SLIRP) are in the 2026 panel; this run measures the K562->hESC transfer problem, not per-target submission decisions.
cost_note: Actual billing not exposed by retrieved CLI metadata. Function timeout was raised to 3600s for the 47-target run; the planning envelope is approximately $0.44/hour at recorded Modal rates.

findings.generator_calibration: Null champion transport on eval controls: variance ratio 1.047 - the transport generator is well-calibrated on unperturbed cells; dispersion is not the primary defect.
findings.borrowed_signature_quality: Borrowed K562 deltas (delta_scale=1.7): mean cosine 0.179, median 0.268 vs measured-delta transport median 0.514 and observed fit-split ceiling median 0.701. Borrowed beats measured in only 1/32 targets; 11/32 borrowed cosines <0.1 and 8 are negative (actively wrong direction).
findings.transferability_gate_falsified: corr(cos(delta_k562, delta_hesc), borrowed_cosine) = 0.219 overall and 0.322 among high-ceiling targets (obs>0.6). A precomputable per-target gate from the paired source deltas does NOT reliably predict which borrowed signatures transfer; the paired cosine itself is weak across the board (median ~0.10, max 0.37), consistent with prior LOO ~0.13.
findings.amplitude_ratio: ||delta_hesc||/||delta_k562|| median 1.09 (mean 1.57) in the paired training corpus - within-corpus hESC signature norms are comparable to K562, though this is a different measurement from the k013 lineage-ratio estimate (~0.44) that motivated context C down-scaling.
findings.conclusion: Signature content is the quantified bottleneck (median cosine gap 0.27 borrowed vs 0.51 measured), and no cheap per-target gate exists in the paired source data. Uniform levers (delta_scale, kd_std, context amplitudes) and gate-based selection are exhausted; remaining routes are context-matched signature content (lineage-matched corpora, which do not cover this panel) or a learned transfer model (Track 2).
